title: Hancock County Round 11 brownfield awards
warnings: Three awards to TWO different recipients. Two are the City of Findlay; the Bluffton Former Gas America assessment is awarded to the HANCOCK COUNTY COMMISSIONERS OFFICE, not the City. `amount_usd` below is the county-wide Round 11 total; the per-project rows are the awards.

This packet is the AWARD-DESCRIPTION document distributed with the announcement. It is not a grant agreement and carries no agreement number, execution date, or disbursement terms; none are asserted here.

The job figures are the packet's own forward-looking expectations for each redevelopment ("expected to create 24 jobs, retain 28 positions"), not outcomes. They are recorded as stated projections, not as employment on the record.
Hancock County's presence in Rounds 4-10 of this program is [open] — not researched here. The "Round 11" framing below says nothing about whether the county was awarded in earlier rounds.

fields.agency: State of Ohio (announced by the Governor's office, 2026-05-13); program administered by the Ohio Department of Development
fields.borrower: City of Findlay (2 awards) and Hancock County Commissioners Office (1 award)
fields.note: [verified] Three Hancock County brownfield awards totalling $999,998 were announced in Round 11 on 2026-05-13: $663,998 to remediate the former Lincoln Elementary School in Findlay, $238,000 to assess an abandoned Tiffin Avenue gas station, and $98,000 to the county for a BUSTR assessment at a former Gas America station in Bluffton. Two of the three are petroleum underground-storage-tank sites; the third is asbestos in a vacant school.

title: Hancock County Flood-Risk Reduction Program — Eagle Creek Dry Storage Basin + Blanchard River benching
warnings: The FEMA.gov primary release (and the City of Findlay obligation notice, News/1818) returned HTTP 403; all dollar/parcel/acre figures are corroborated across 13abc.com, spectrumlocalnews.com and Rep. Latta's release (wktn.com), not read byte-verbatim from FEMA.gov. High confidence, multiply sourced; re-capture the FEMA release + city notice from a non-datacenter IP to lock the primary text.

FLOODWAY vs FLOODPLAIN — do not conflate. This FEMA release counts "1,290 parcels and 1,500 acres removed from the regulatory FLOODWAY" (13abc / spectrum). The Eagle Creek basin project page counts "approximately 1,830 parcels and 1,400 acres from the regulatory FLOODPLAIN" (hancockcountyflooding.com). Different regulatory zones AND different numbers; both preserved below. The Phase-I LOMR's SFHA accounting (375 removed / 985 reduced) is a third, separate metric.

Do NOT merge the November-2024 CONDITIONAL-approval reporting (hometownstations/WLIO, "November 15, 2024," funds "within 6 to 9 months") into this record. This is the 2026-04-22 FINAL obligation that unlocked summer-2026 bidding — a distinct event.

title: Michigan Sugar Company Findlay warehouse
warnings: The employer expressly disclaims that WARN was triggered — "Although we do not believe the closure required any notice, we are sending this as a courtesy." This is a COURTESY filing. Treating it as a statutory WARN trigger would misstate the employer's own position; four employees is far below the federal threshold.

No final day of operations is stated. The letter says it "has yet to be determined." The only fixed date is that the two BCTGM-represented employees "will remain on our active roll until January 31, 2026". No closure date is asserted here.

Three notification dates appear and are distinct: verbal notice to employees 2025-12-04, written notice to BCTGM Local 19 on 2025-12-03, written notice to the two represented employees on 2025-12-11. They are recorded separately below rather than collapsed.

title: Blanchard River Watershed, Ohio — Feasibility Report
warnings: The LRD source page 403'd on direct WebFetch and on curl (Akamai "Access Denied"); the body was obtained via a reader proxy (r.jina.ai). Treat the verbatim string and the 2024-01-11 date as reader-proxy-recovered, not a clean primary read — the article should be re-captured from a non-datacenter IP to lock byte-verbatim text.

Whether the 2024-01-11 Review Plan signals a RENEWED/active federal feasibility effort or is an archival closeout is an [inference] from the document type (a Review Plan is USACE QA/peer-review scoping, normally produced at the START of a feasibility study) and its title ("Feasibility Study of flood risk management and ecosystem restorations plans"). The page states no "active / renewed / archival" status in words.

The 2015 USACE recommended plan ("Western Diversion of Eagle Creek") is characterized as having a NEGATIVE benefit-cost ratio in the program FAQ, but no NUMERIC 2015 BCR is public in any source reached. Do NOT confuse that failed federal BCR with the LOCAL program's own 2.94 BCR (the 2018 Jack Faucett Associates / Stantec analysis) — two different studies.

The locally-funded program (MWCD / Stantec, FEMA FMA + ODNR + Ohio Capital Budget) proceeded independently of the federal study.

title: Maumee Watershed Nutrient TMDL — Findlay WPCF total-phosphorus wasteload allocation
warnings: The 3.2 metric tons (Table A4.1) and the 3,200 kg (OHP000001 Part IV.A.1) are the SAME allocation stated in two units by two instruments, not two allocations. Do not add them.

Table A4.5's seven numeric columns are, in order, 2008 / WLA / 2017 / 2018 / 2019 / 2020 / 2021. The first column is a 2008 baseline load and the second is the allocation — reading the row left-to-right as a time series would misreport both.

The most recent per-facility spring load on this record is 2021. The 2024 Biennial Report publishes only the BASIN GROUP total, not Findlay's own load, so no post-2021 Findlay figure is asserted here. Whether Findlay is still over its allocation is [open] — the annual Season Report required by OHP000001 Part IV.D is the record that would answer it (a records-request lead).

fields.facility: Findlay Water Pollution Control Center (WPCC/WPCF), NPDES 2PD00008 / OH0025135
fields.site_address: 1201 South River Road, Findlay, OH 45840, Hancock County

fields.affected_resource: Blanchard River (RM 56.42) → Auglaize River → Maumee River → Lake Erie Western Basin
fields.note: [verified] Findlay WPCF's spring-season total-phosphorus wasteload allocation is 3.2 metric tons (3,200 kg), and its reported spring loads for every year on the TMDL's own record — 2017 through 2021 — were 4.8, 5.5, 5.3, 5.5 and 5.4 metric tons. Its 2008 baseline load, 4.4 MT, was also above it. The allocation is enforced not through the plant's individual permit but through the Maumee Watershed Total Phosphorus general permit OHP000001, whose compliance rule (Part IV.C.3) makes an individual exceedance a violation ONLY when the 39-facility CUMULATIVE load also exceeds its cap. In the 2024 spring season the group reported 43,304 kg against a 64,170 kg cap — 20,866 kg of headroom — so an over-allocation Findlay load was not, on that record, a violation of anything.
